qt: to the Commission Sakis Arnaoutoglou (S&D) Subject:

In August 2026, the Benaki Phytopathological Institute confirmed that the Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri) had been detected for the first time in Greece in an orange orchard in Rhodes. This insect acts as a vector for the transmission of bacteria that cause the devastating disease Huanglongbing (HLB), also known as ‘citrus greening disease’, for which there is no effective treatment. According to the Greek authorities, these bacteria have not been detected in the country. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2247 already provides for mandatory annual surveys, while the specific requirement for statistically sound planning and sampling, in accordance with Article 3(2) thereof, will apply from 1 January 2029. Given the importance of Greek citrus fruit production, can the Commission say: 1.
What are the latest reported findings of the checks in Rhodes?
How does it assess the adequacy of checks in Greece, particularly in large citrus production areas?
What immediate technical and financial support can it provide for enhanced checks and laboratory testing and to prevent the spread of the disease through the movement of plants?
